newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak central bank offers repo, liquidity tight.
newsitem.headline: Slovak central bank offers repo, liquidity tight.

text.p: The National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) said on Friday it would hold a three-day repo tender with a fixed amount offered of one billion crowns.

"The amount shows the central bank decided to continue in its strategy of limiting crown liquidity on the money market in order to prevent pressure on the currency," NBS chief dealer Peter Andresic told Reuters.
But Andresic said that bank liquidity in payment relations with clients was at a sufficient level.
According to NBS figures the Slovak banking sector lacked 7.14 percent of required funds to meet minimum reserves requirements as of May 29.

"It is now sure that the sector as such will not meet the reserves requirements today, but the NBS must look at more important things at the moment, such as currency stability," said one Bratislava based' trader.
He said that the central bank would not move too strictly against banks unable to meet the reserve requirements.

The NBS has been deliberately keeping the local money market short of liquidity over the past two weeks to prevent access to crown funds that could be used for speculative selling and spark a fall in the crown.
